core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 3763-3772): with injective transition maps the colimit presheaf is separated, its sheafification is the colimit of the sheaves, and the plus construction is injective on separated presheaves, so the canonical map is injective.

Part (2) (proof lines 3775-3793): sections are written as maps from the final sheaf, two compatible families are compared by forming the equalizers of their stages, the equalizer of the colimit maps is the filtered colimit of the stagewise equalizers, and quasi-compactness of the final sheaf converts the surjectivity of the displayed coproduct onto the equalizer into the existence of a stage where the two maps already agree.

Part (3) (proof lines 3797-3802): assuming both hypotheses, a map into the colimit pulls back the stages to a filtered family of subsheaves of the final sheaf whose colimit is everything, so by quasi-compactness one stage already is everything, which is exactly surjectivity.

Part (4) (proof lines 3805-3869): the hypotheses on the set S produce a quasi-compact object with a surjection onto the final sheaf, hence injectivity by part (2); surjectivity is then obtained by lifting the final sheaf through the coproduct of the stages, factoring through finitely many stages using quasi-compactness, and applying the equalizer argument of part (2) to the quasi-compact product of the chosen object with itself.
proof_roadmap: Prove injectivity both under injective transition maps and under quasi-compactness by an equalizer argument.
Deduce bijectivity when both hypotheses hold by showing that a map into the colimit is already defined at some stage.
Under the additional hypothesis on the set S, produce a quasi-compact object covering the final sheaf and repeat the equalizer argument for it and its square.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four statements about the canonical map from the filtered colimit of the global sections of a filtered diagram of sheaves of sets into the global sections of its colimit: injectivity under injective transition maps, injectivity over a quasi-compact topos, bijectivity when both hold, and bijectivity under an additional hypothesis on a set of objects of the topos (statement lines 3731-3760). The proof treats each part: part (1) via separated presheaves and the plus construction (proof lines 3763-3772); part (2) by forming the equalizers of two compatible families and using that the equalizer of the colimit maps is the filtered colimit of the stagewise equalizers together with quasi-compactness of the final sheaf (proof lines 3775-3793); part (3) by pulling the stages back along a map into the colimit and using quasi-compactness (proof lines 3797-3802); and part (4) by producing a quasi-compact object surjecting onto the final sheaf, factoring a lift through finitely many stages, and repeating the equalizer argument for its square (proof lines 3805-3869). The non-formal content is the equalizer bookkeeping with the quasi-compactness input. The claim is H2: several written-out arguments with each input named.
